headline: 57 rescued in Teknaf: Army soldier killed in gunfight with human traffickers
summary: A joint force operation in the hills of Teknaf rescued 57 hostages, but a 27-year-old soldier was killed after being shot in the shoulder.
details: A 27-year-old soldier, Md. Titas Sheikh, aşken during a joint force operation against human traffickers in the Teknaf upazila of Cox's Bazar.

caption:
57 hostages rescued, but at a heavy cost. A 27-year-old soldier has died after a gunfight with human traffickers in Teknaf.

A 27-year-old soldier, Md. Titas Sheikh, aşken during a joint force operation against human traffickers in the Teknaf upazila of Cox's Bazar.

The operation took place around 5 PM on Thursday in the deep hills of the Rangikhali area. A joint team consisting of the Army's 10th Infantry Division, Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), and local police was deployed based on intelligence regarding a gang of 15-16 armed traffickers.

According to the ISPR, the traffickers opened fire on the joint force upon sensing their presence. A gunfight ensued, during which Soldier Md. Titas Sheikh was shot in the left shoulder.

The soldier was initially given primary treatment at a nearby hospital before being moved to the Combined Military Hospital (CMH) in Ramu for advanced care, where he was declared dead.

The joint force successfully rescued 57 people, including Rohingya and Bangladeshi citizens, who were being held hostage by the traffickers.

topic: govt plans december start for malaysia worker flights
headline_marked: Govt eyes [[worker flights to Malaysia to resume in December]]
headline: Govt eyes worker flights to Malaysia to resume in December
summary: The first few flights will carry workers free of charge, with the government planning to waive all service charges for initial recruits.
details: Expatriates' Welfare Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury announced that the government hopes to resume sending workers to Malaysia by December. The first few flights are expected to carry workers free of charge.
The initial workers will be sent through the state-run recruitment agency, Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Limited (BOESL), which has already published a recruitment notice.
Minister Ariful stated that the government would waive all service charges and is considering an online application process followed by a lottery system to select workers.
During a meeting with recruiting agents, a proposal was made to cap migration costs for privately recruited workers between Tk 250,000 and Tk 300,000, which the minister welcomed.
The government aims to ensure that all legally registered recruiting agencies have equal opportunities, preventing the business from being concentrated among a few agencies.
The minister expressed hope that a new Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Malaysia would be signed by December.
Plans are also underway to establish dedicated support cells in Malaysia and Saudi Arabia to help workers resolve problems after they go abroad.
The medical examination fee for Malaysia-bound workers has been fixed at Tk 8,000. Agencies found charging more will face license cancellation and legal action.
caption:
Workers can head to Malaysia for free! The government plans to resume flights in December with initial flights free of charge.

Expatriates' Welfare Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury announced that the government hopes to resume sending workers to Malaysia by December. The first few flights are expected to carry workers free of charge.

The initial workers will be sent through the state-run recruitment agency, Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Limited (BOESL), which has already published a recruitment notice.

Minister Ariful stated that the government would waive all service charges and is considering an online application process followed by a lottery system to select workers.

During a meeting with recruiting agents, a proposal was made to cap migration costs for privately recruited workers between Tk 250,000 and Tk 300,000, which the minister welcomed.

The government aims to ensure that all legally registered recruiting agencies have equal opportunities, preventing the business from being concentrated among a few agencies.

The minister expressed hope that a new Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Malaysia would be signed by December.

Plans are also underway to establish dedicated support cells in Malaysia and Saudi Arabia to help workers resolve problems after they go abroad.

The medical examination fee for Malaysia-bound workers has been fixed at Tk 8,000. Agencies found charging more will face license cancellation and legal action.
